mergedParams.userDescription: Smooth gradient wipe. internal effects for text, video, images

output.title: Smooth Gradient Wipe - Text, Video & Image Effects

prompts.prompt: Create an internal effect preset for a smooth gradient wipe that reveals content by animating a CSS linear-gradient mask from left to right. The effect should use clip-path with a gradient-like transition by animating multiple overlapping rectangles with staggered opacity transitions, creating a smooth wipe effect. Accept parameters for wipeDirection (left/right/up/down), duration (ms), and gradientSoftness (0-1 for hard to soft edge). Use generic AnimationRange effects with ease-in-out easing. The effect should target any component by ID and create a cinematic reveal similar to video editing wipe transitions.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: Generic AnimationRange[]. Properties: opacity + clipPath polygon animation. Structure: Multiple staggered opacity keyframes (prog: 0->1) with clipPath rectangles. Effect data: { type: 'generic', mode: 'provider', targetIds: [inputId], start: 0, duration: inputDuration, ranges: [{key: 'opacity', val: [0,1], prog: [0,1]}, {key: 'clipPath', val: ['polygon(0 0, 0% 0, 0% 100%, 0 100%)', 'polygon(0 0, 100% 0, 100% 100%, 0 100%)'], prog: [0,1]}]}. Input schema: z.object({ targetId: z.string(), direction: z.enum(['left','right','up','down']), duration: z.number().default(1000), softness: z.number().min(0).max(1).default(0.3) }). Return: { effects: [effectData] }

prompts.prompt: Build an internal effect preset for an audio-reactive gradient wipe that synchronizes the wipe progression with bass beats in the audio track. The effect should create a pulsing gradient reveal that moves across the target element in sync with the music's rhythm. Use waveform effects to modulate the wipe speed and intensity based on bass frequency analysis. Include parameters for baseSpeed, beatSensitivity, and wipeAngle (diagonal wipes). The gradient should pulse its softness with the beat while progressing across the element, creating a dynamic music-driven reveal effect perfect for music videos or beat-synced content.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: Waveform (audio-reactive). Properties: translateX + scale + opacity with bass modulation. Waveform config: { type: 'translate', audioProperty: 'bass', sensitivity: inputSensitivity, threshold: 0.3 }. Combined with generic opacity gradient. Effect data: [{ type: 'waveform', mode: 'provider', targetIds: [inputId], start: 0, duration: inputDuration, props: { type: 'translate', audioProperty: 'bass', axis: 'x', intensity: 100, sensitivity: 0.8 }}, { type: 'generic', ranges: [{key: 'opacity', val: [0,0.5,1], prog: [0,0.3,1]}]}]. Input schema: z.object({ targetId: z.string(), baseSpeed: z.number().default(1), beatSensitivity: z.number().min(0).max(1).default(0.7), wipeAngle: z.number().default(0) }). Return: { effects: [...waveformEffect, ...genericEffect] }

prompts.prompt: Design an internal effect preset for a multi-layer gradient wipe that creates depth by animating three separate gradient layers with different timings and blur levels. Each layer should have a slightly different wipe speed and softness, creating a volumetric reveal effect. The front layer wipes fastest with sharp edges, middle layer follows with medium blur, and back layer wipes slowest with heavy blur. Accept parameters for layerCount, depthOffset (timing difference between layers), and blurIntensity. This creates a cinematic depth-of-field wipe effect similar to high-end video production transitions.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: Combined (multiple generic effects). Properties: opacity + blur + transform for each layer. Structure: Array of 3 effect objects with staggered timings. Effect data: layers.map((i) => ({ type: 'generic', mode: 'provider', targetIds: [`${inputId}-layer-${i}`], start: i * depthOffset, duration: baseDuration, ranges: [{key: 'opacity', val: [0,1], prog: [0,1]}, {key: 'blur', val: [blurIntensity * i, 0], prog: [0,1]}, {key: 'translateX', val: [-50 * i, 0], prog: [0,1]}] })). Input schema: z.object({ targetId: z.string(), layerCount: z.number().min(2).max(5).default(3), depthOffset: z.number().default(200), blurIntensity: z.number().default(5) }). Return: { effects: [...layerEffects] }

prompts.prompt: Create an internal effect preset for a color gradient wipe that transitions through a spectrum of colors while revealing the content. The wipe should animate both opacity and a color overlay that shifts from one color to another as it progresses. Include support for custom color stops and the ability to follow a specific color palette. Parameters should include startColor, endColor, colorStops array, and wipePattern (linear/radial/conic). The effect should use CSS gradients and blend modes to create a vibrant, artistic reveal that works especially well with monochrome or desaturated base content.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: Generic AnimationRange[]. Properties: opacity + backgroundColor + filter (hue-rotate). Structure: Keyframes for gradient color animation. Effect data: { type: 'generic', mode: 'provider', targetIds: [inputId], start: 0, duration: inputDuration, ranges: [{key: 'opacity', val: [0,0.7,1], prog: [0,0.5,1]}, {key: 'backgroundColor', val: colorStops.map(c => c.color), prog: colorStops.map(c => c.position)}, {key: 'filter', val: ['hue-rotate(0deg)', 'hue-rotate(180deg)', 'hue-rotate(360deg)'], prog: [0,0.5,1]}] }. Input schema: z.object({ targetId: z.string(), startColor: z.string(), endColor: z.string(), colorStops: z.array(z.object({ color: z.string(), position: z.number() })), wipePattern: z.enum(['linear','radial','conic']) }). Return: { effects: [effectData] }

prompts.prompt: Build an internal effect preset for a displacement gradient wipe that uses transform skewing and perspective to create a 3D wipe effect. The content should appear to fold and unfold along the wipe edge, creating a page-turn or curtain-like reveal. Include parameters for perspective depth, skewAngle, and foldDirection. The effect should animate rotateY/rotateX with perspective transform, combined with opacity gradient for smooth edges. This creates a sophisticated dimensional wipe perfect for premium transitions between sections or revealing important content with dramatic flair.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: Generic AnimationRange[]. Properties: rotateY + perspective + skew + opacity. Structure: 3D transform keyframes with perspective. Effect data: { type: 'generic', mode: 'provider', targetIds: [inputId], start: 0, duration: inputDuration, ranges: [{key: 'rotateY', val: [90, 45, 0], prog: [0, 0.5, 1]}, {key: 'perspective', val: [inputPerspective], prog: [0]}, {key: 'skew', val: [`skewY(${skewAngle}deg)`, 'skewY(0deg)'], prog: [0, 1]}, {key: 'opacity', val: [0, 0.8, 1], prog: [0, 0.3, 1]}] }. Input schema: z.object({ targetId: z.string(), perspectiveDepth: z.number().default(1000), skewAngle: z.number().default(15), foldDirection: z.enum(['horizontal','vertical','diagonal']) }). Return: { effects: [effectData] }

prompts.prompt: Design an internal effect preset for a particle gradient wipe where the content appears to materialize from scattered particles that coalesce along a gradient line. The effect should animate multiple small elements (pseudo-particles) with randomized positions that converge to form the final content. Include parameters for particleCount, scatterRadius, and convergencePattern. Each particle should have slightly different timing and easing for organic movement. This creates a dissolve-like wipe effect similar to digital disintegration/integration effects used in sci-fi productions.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: Combined (multiple generic effects with randomization). Properties: translateX/Y + scale + opacity for particles. Structure: Array of particle effects with random offsets. Effect data: particles.map((i) => ({ type: 'generic', mode: 'provider', targetIds: [`${inputId}-particle-${i}`], start: Math.random() * 200, duration: baseDuration, ranges: [{key: 'translateX', val: [Math.random() * scatterRadius - scatterRadius/2, 0], prog: [0, 1]}, {key: 'translateY', val: [Math.random() * scatterRadius - scatterRadius/2, 0], prog: [0, 1]}, {key: 'scale', val: [0, 1], prog: [0, 1]}, {key: 'opacity', val: [0, 1], prog: [0.2, 1]}] })). Input schema: z.object({ targetId: z.string(), particleCount: z.number().default(20), scatterRadius: z.number().default(200), convergencePattern: z.enum(['center','edge','random']) }). Return: { effects: [...particleEffects] }

prompts.prompt: Create an internal effect preset for a gradient wipe with dynamic edge distortion that warbles and waves as it progresses across the content. The wipe edge should have an animated wave pattern using sin/cos functions to create an organic, liquid-like reveal. Include parameters for waveAmplitude, waveFrequency, and waveSpeed. The effect should use SVG filters or CSS custom properties to create the distortion along the gradient edge, making it appear as if the content is being revealed by a flowing liquid or energy field.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: Generic AnimationRange[] with calculated wave values. Properties: clipPath (with wave calculation) + filter (turbulence). Structure: Dynamic clipPath with sine wave edge. Effect data: { type: 'generic', mode: 'provider', targetIds: [inputId], start: 0, duration: inputDuration, ranges: [{key: 'clipPath', val: waveFrames.map(f => `polygon(${f})`), prog: linearProgress}, {key: 'filter', val: ['url(#turbulence)', 'none'], prog: [0, 1]}, {key: 'opacity', val: [0, 0.5, 1], prog: [0, 0.2, 1]}] }. Wave calculation: Math.sin(x * frequency + time * speed) * amplitude. Input schema: z.object({ targetId: z.string(), waveAmplitude: z.number().default(30), waveFrequency: z.number().default(0.02), waveSpeed: z.number().default(2) }). Return: { effects: [effectData] }

prompts.prompt: Build an internal effect preset for a chromatic aberration gradient wipe that splits RGB channels and offsets them during the wipe progression. The effect should separate red, green, and blue channels with different wipe timings and positions, creating a glitch-like prismatic reveal. Include parameters for channelOffset (pixel spread), aberrationIntensity, and glitchFrequency. The channels should converge as the wipe completes, transitioning from distorted separation to clean final state. This creates a tech-inspired wipe perfect for modern, edgy content transitions.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: Combined (RGB channel effects). Properties: translateX/Y + opacity + filter for each channel. Structure: Three separate effects for R, G, B channels. Effect data: ['red', 'green', 'blue'].map((channel, i) => ({ type: 'generic', mode: 'provider', targetIds: [`${inputId}-${channel}`], start: i * 50, duration: inputDuration, ranges: [{key: 'translateX', val: [channelOffset * (i-1), 0], prog: [0, 1]}, {key: 'opacity', val: [0, 0.8, 1], prog: [0, 0.3, 1]}, {key: 'filter', val: [`blur(${2-i}px)`, 'blur(0px)'], prog: [0, 1]}] })). Input schema: z.object({ targetId: z.string(), channelOffset: z.number().default(10), aberrationIntensity: z.number().min(0).max(1).default(0.5), glitchFrequency: z.number().default(0) }). Return: { effects: [...channelEffects] }

prompts.prompt: Design an internal effect preset for a radial gradient wipe that emanates from customizable origin points, creating circular or elliptical reveal patterns. The gradient should support multiple origin points for complex multi-source wipes, with each origin having its own timing and intensity. Include parameters for originPoints array, wipeShape (circle/ellipse), and expansionCurve (linear/exponential/ease). The effect should animate scale transforms from each origin with gradient opacity masks, creating ripple-like reveals perfect for emphasizing focal points or creating dramatic center-stage reveals.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: Combined (multiple radial effects). Properties: scale + opacity with radial masks. Structure: Array of radial expansion effects from origins. Effect data: originPoints.map((origin, i) => ({ type: 'generic', mode: 'provider', targetIds: [`${inputId}-radial-${i}`], start: origin.delay || 0, duration: inputDuration, ranges: [{key: 'scale', val: [0, 1], prog: [0, 1]}, {key: 'transformOrigin', val: [`${origin.x}% ${origin.y}%`], prog: [0]}, {key: 'opacity', val: [0, 1], prog: [0, 0.5]}, {key: 'maskImage', val: [`radial-gradient(circle at ${origin.x}% ${origin.y}%, transparent 0%, black 100%)`], prog: [0]}] })). Input schema: z.object({ targetId: z.string(), originPoints: z.array(z.object({ x: z.number(), y: z.number(), delay: z.number().optional() })), wipeShape: z.enum(['circle','ellipse']), expansionCurve: z.enum(['linear','exponential','ease']) }). Return: { effects: [...radialEffects] }

prompts.prompt: Create an internal effect preset for a gradient wipe with variable speed that accelerates and decelerates based on content density or custom speed curves. The wipe should analyze target zones and adjust its progression speed, slowing down over important areas and speeding through transitions. Include parameters for speedCurve array, slowZones array (regions to emphasize), and adaptiveSpeed boolean. The effect should use custom easing functions and variable duration segments to create a dynamic wipe that responds to content importance, perfect for highlighting key information while maintaining smooth overall flow.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: Generic AnimationRange[] with custom timing. Properties: clipPath + opacity with variable progression. Structure: Segmented animation with custom speed zones. Effect data: { type: 'generic', mode: 'provider', targetIds: [inputId], start: 0, duration: calculateVariableDuration(speedCurve, slowZones), ranges: [{key: 'clipPath', val: speedCurve.map(s => `inset(0 ${100-s.position}% 0 0)`), prog: speedCurve.map(s => s.progress)}, {key: 'opacity', val: [0, ...slowZones.map(() => 0.8), 1], prog: [0, ...slowZones.map(z => z.position), 1]}] }. Speed calculation: Adjust prog values based on slowZones positions. Input schema: z.object({ targetId: z.string(), speedCurve: z.array(z.object({ position: z.number(), progress: z.number(), speed: z.number() })), slowZones: z.array(z.object({ start: z.number(), end: z.number(), factor: z.number() })), adaptiveSpeed: z.boolean().default(false) }). Return: { effects: [effectData] }
